notes:
Adds an opt-in route for Google AI. Gemini, AI Studio and Google sign-in refuse requests that arrive from a Cloudflare address, so a user in a country Gemini supports still sees "not available in your region". The refusal arrives inside TLS after the TCP connection succeeds, so the existing proxy fallback never saw a failure to retry. Under Proxy / CDN, "Send Google AI traffic through the proxy" sends only those few hostnames through the exit the operator configured; everything else stays direct. It needs a PROXYIP or proxy chain of your own and is ignored on the shared public fallback, because sign-in should not go through a server the operator did not choose. If that exit is unreachable the affected hosts fall back to a genuine direct connection rather than to a third party, so nothing breaks, though the region problem returns until it recovers.

The forced-host matcher, which this feature reuses, had two long-standing faults. It treated a dot in a pattern as a regex wildcard, so the shipped scholar.google.com entry also matched lookalike hostnames, and it rebuilt a regular expression per pattern on every connection. Patterns are now compiled once, escaped, and capped at three wildcards, which closes a path where one mistyped entry in an operator list let any user of that panel exhaust the isolate CPU.

The build now refuses to produce an artifact that imports a node: module while a wrangler config omits nodejs_compat. A Worker deployed without that flag fails to evaluate and answers 1101 on every route including /healthz, which is indistinguishable from an account-level block and cost a release to diagnose. Every wrangler config in the repository is checked, not just the default one.

Also in this release: share links advertise ALPN when the operator sets one, the Google Apps Script relay is gone, and seven unused functions and three unreferenced bundled assets have been removed.
